title: What do Coppola's last three movies tell us & why this is his best period since the 70s?

commenti.body: Coppola hasn’t made a good film since 1986, Peggy Sue. Captain EO was a depressing sign of selling out and losing his artistic integrity. Godfather III was the nail in his coffin. The cast list for Megalopolis is concerning. It’s a **lot** of actors trying to pull a Norma Desmond. I hope you enjoy it, but I don’t have high hopes.

It's a perception that I respect. But Copolla's filmography of recent years is very well received by European critics, particularly in France. And it is more and more revalued, perhaps because of the politics of the authors and/or because of current American cinematographic production. Talking about Coppola's artistic integrity when he is probably one of the freest director since he self-produced seems inappropriate to me

Tucker, the man and his dream (1988) is a fantastic film and one of Coppola's best. Its able to talk about art, vision, ingenuity in a capitalist world. Truly one of his best and im personally very excited for his new picture

I've heard that Coppola has developed a great late career style but I haven't watched anything past Dracula yet, but I'm curious to. Also I think his last 3 films is the first time after '82 that he can choose his own projects because he's no longer in debt.
Eh, I really love his 80’s work. The outsiders , Rumble Fish (personal favorite of his filmography, Peggy Sue Got Married, and the Cotton Club. I think it holds up with his 70’s output.

I also like this period of Coppola, despite the constraints of the studios they remain very personal films of very high quality. Basically what people bitterly criticize Coppola for is that he no longer made large-scale films. It's as trivial as that IMO. He has always been an excellent visual artist with an elegant style and perfect mastery. I think that Coppola could easily copy the styles of other great directors like Scorsese (whom I really like) but that the opposite is not true. This will also mean that ultimately Coppola is very little appreciated and mainly by the American public ; sad !

People talk about it like it was a humongous drop in quality on par with Richard Kelly or Dario Argento. Maybe I’d agree once he moved onto Jack in the mid 90’s but I agree his recent films show he hasn’t lost his touch artistically. He’s just not working with the same resources.

Coppola's entire career has been defined by brief moments of recognition broken up by protracted periods of struggle. I don't thing the American public has ever *really* understood or appreciated him.
